Definition: from a derivative of G450 (in the sense of removal); properly, to drive out of home, i.e. (by implication) to disturb (literally or figuratively):--trouble, turn upside down, make an uproar.
BiblicalUsage: The word means to turn upside down, to drive out of house and home: the rulers of Thessalonica cried, 'These that have turned the world upside down are come hither also' — and Paul wishes those who trouble the Galatians were even cut off. It is the uproar the gospel causes: the world turned upside down, and the troublers who ought to be cut off.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for turning upside down carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the charge — the world turned upside down, and the accusers meant it as a complaint when it was really a compliment.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
